title: Visible Light Positioning as a Next-Generation Indoor Positioning Technology: A Tutorial
domain: Visible Light Positioning / Indoor Localization / Optical Wireless

analysis_policy.focus: Comprehensive tutorial extraction with emphasis on system design, component taxonomy, localization algorithms, and practical deployment guidance
analysis_policy.depth: Full paper analysis including all 7 major sections and subsections

normalization.heading_style: Roman numeral major sections (I-VII) with letter subsections (A, B, C)

section_flow.title: Introduction
section_flow.summary: Introduces VLP as next-generation indoor positioning, presents Scopus publication trends, and differentiates this tutorial from existing surveys via comparison table.
key_claims: VLP can provide centimetre-order accuracy at low cost
No appropriate VLP tutorial exists covering all aspects
VLP is a key candidate for 6G wireless networks

section_flow.title: Context
section_flow.summary: Provides comprehensive IPS taxonomy, positions VLP in the technology landscape, discusses LED revolution and LaaS business model, and covers illumination constraints (flicker, glare, uniformity).
key_claims: Indoor LBS is flourishing with 80-90% of human time spent indoors
No dominant IPS standard exists - landscape is fragmented
LED modulation must exceed 3kHz to avoid temporal light artifacts

section_flow.title: Components and Paradigms of VLP Systems
section_flow.summary: Exhaustive taxonomy of VLP components: transmitters (fluorescent, LED, micro-LED, laser), receivers (camera, photodiode, solar cell), propagation models (LOS/NLOS), modulation schemes, and MAC protocols.
key_claims: Small-scale fading is negligible due to sensor area >> wavelength
FDMA is the most common MAC for VLP due to synchronization challenges

section_flow.title: VLP Localization Techniques and Algorithms
section_flow.summary: Covers positioning principles (RSS, TOA, TDOA, AOA) with VLP-specific adaptations, discusses ML approaches, provides mathematical formulations for trilateration and angulation.
key_claims: RSS is the most straightforward and widely-implemented approach for VLP
AOA is inherently more accurate but requires angular diversity receivers
ML approaches achieve cm-level accuracy but require dense training grids

section_flow.title: A Primer on RSS VLP Systems with a Single Photodiode
section_flow.summary: Step-by-step guide for building a single-PD RSS VLP system: hardware selection, signal processing, 9 localization algorithms (trilateration, CMD, weighted LS, fingerprinting, MBF, MLE), and 42m×21m industrial deployment with p50=29cm error.
key_claims: VLP receiver BOM can be as low as €28
Industrial deployment achieved p50=29cm, p75=58cm error
Model-based fingerprinting eliminates need for on-site calibration

section_flow.title: Open Challenges and Future Roadmap
subsections: Opportunities (AI/ML, Hybrid Systems, uVLP, Solar Cells, RIS)
section_flow.summary: Identifies key barriers: LED driver retrofit cost, lack of standardization, receiver tilt sensitivity, non-Lambertian sources. Proposes solutions: AI for calibration, hybrid VLP+UWB, unmodulated VLP, RIS for coverage.
key_claims: No consensus VLP system has been identified
VLP RIS research is nonexistent as of September 2023

section_flow.title: Conclusion
section_flow.summary: Summarizes VLP benefits for smart applications, reiterates tutorial contributions, and emphasizes practical deployment guidance.

rhetorical_contract.delivery_mechanism: Layer-by-layer tutorial structure from IPS context through component taxonomy to practical implementation
rhetorical_contract.unique_contribution: First survey covering all aspects: illumination, transmitter/receiver hardware, modulation, localization, and hands-on primer
